## Requirements: Fixed-column Terminal sizing across Web and App

### Background / product decision (2026-10-26)

Nession is a single persistent tmux Session used sequentially on desktop and phone. Today `ResizeController` derives **both** cols/rows from available pixels and measured xterm cell dimensions, so PC → phone → PC changes the remote column count and causes avoidable horizontal wrapping/reflow. The product direction is now **one fixed logical column count for a Session on every device**, while **CSS font size / rendered cell metrics** fit each viewport width and **rows** follow usable viewport height.

This is a **new product decision superseding only the width/column-sizing policy** in completed #2286 (which explicitly requested dynamic cols), NOT a claim that #2286 was never implemented. Retain its active-device ControlLease, generation fencing, authoritative resize timeline, ordered parser writer, PTY SIGWINCH, and P2P/Relay parity. Related terminal fidelity: #2283, #1645, #1490, #1503, #2464. Existing xterm `gridFor()` and resize path must be reviewed, not wrapped with a competing resize owner.

### Desired contract

1. **Canonical cols**: One configurable/project-owned integer `terminalCols` (candidate **88**, *not approved yet*) becomes the active Session's immutable width across Web/App and ordinary viewport resize/takeover. Simulator explores 70–120 incl. 80/88/96/100/120; select the actual production default after reviewing device evidence. Changing the project's default must not silently change an already-running Session's width.
2. **Web width/typography**: Use the existing JetBrains Mono Variable font; select a comfortable maximum Web font (candidate **14 CSS px**) and derive **terminal maximum content width** as `cols × measured xterm cell width`, plus owned horizontal insets. On large windows center/cap width; sidebar expanded/collapsed or narrow windows only change *font size as needed* and available rows, not cols. Do not stretch glyphs or change their aspect ratio.
3. **App/mobile**: The same canonical cols fit the actual available **content box** (respect safe area/padding), with a smaller, possibly fractional CSS font size. Use xterm's actual measured cell metrics, not the approximate `fontSize × 0.6` as production truth. No CSS `transform:scale()` of the terminal (mouse-cell coordinate drift). Explicitly validate very small mobile fonts and iOS minimum render/legibility; allow iterative selection of the global column count instead of forcing 88/100/120.
4. **Height/rows**: Recalculate only `rows = floor(usableHeight / measuredCellHeight)` when height changes (window, mobile toolbar/IME, orientation, Capsule chrome), with min-valid rows. Send `(fixedCols, latestRows)` to Agent/tmux **only by authorized Controller**; do not emit duplicate/provisional resize. Resize and terminal output remain in the established serial/ordered stream. Font changes that alter row height must recompute rows after font load.
5. **Cross-device invariants**: PC → iPhone Pro/Pro Max → PC uses the **same cols** in local xterm and actual tmux pane (`stty size`), with the active-device rows. Background observers cannot seize control via ResizeObserver. Width-driven horizontal rewrap should disappear; legitimate TUI rerender, vertical scrollback shifts, partial checkpoints and alt-screen/cursor recovery remain independent behaviors and must not be misrepresented as solved.
6. **Mobile interaction**: Touch, click-to-cell, selection, scrollback and IME must remain correctly mapped to real rendered cells at the smaller font. Retain xterm interaction/mode ownership and existing `TerminalInteractionController`; no Web/App input protocol fork.
7. **Design authority**: Typography metrics come from Experience/design tokens, not hardcoded breakpoint percentage tables. Real cell metrics (including late font loading / DPR) gate the first resize. Document the resulting font-size lower bound and accessibility/fallback policy.

### Build-time configuration (2026-10-27 addition)

The final **fixed column count** and **Web maximum/preferred terminal font size (CSS px)** must both be **optional, explicit build-time inputs**. Updating either should not require changing source code.

- **Suggested contract (illustrative names; implementation follows canonical build config ownership):** `VITE_NESSION_TERMINAL_COLS` (positive integer) and `VITE_NESSION_TERMINAL_WEB_FONT_SIZE` (positive CSS px, may be fractional). Read once at Web/App bundle build time, validate, and emit one typed, immutable client configuration. If omitted, fall back to the versioned defaults selected after prototype review; invalid/out-of-range inputs must fail the build visibly, rather than silently adjust values.
- **One cols source:** Web and mobile use the **same embedded cols**. The Web font input controls only the preferred/max Web CSS font size; the mobile font is still calculated from available viewport width and shared cols. Do not introduce a separate mobile cols value or a mobile fixed-font setting.
- **Bundle/deployment semantics:** Changes to build inputs affect **newly built frontend artifacts**, not previously built static bundles. Document the knobs and expose effective values in build output/diagnostics. No CLI Git mutation or in-app configuration panel is required. Server **does** need runtime environment values sourced from the selected build/release parameters as described below; changing GitHub Variables without rebuilding/redeploying must not silently change live Sessions.
- **Cross-version Session behavior:** An existing live Session must not silently change width solely because a newer frontend build has different defaults; attach/control handoff must resolve the Session's authoritative cols or require an explicit reconfiguration flow, retaining ControlLease and ordered resize/stream guarantees. No independent backend-only columns **policy**: the Server env derives from the same build/release config source and becomes authoritative for new Sessions under the compatibility policy.
- **Tests:** Build two configurations, e.g. `80 cols / 13px` and `96 cols / 14px`, inspect emitted settings and Web/App layout, default fallback and fail-fast invalid cases. Verify changing only Web font input does not alter cols or mobile font policy.


### Server and deployment environment configuration (2026-10-27 addition)

**Build parameter → release artifact / deployment manifest → process environment → Server (and Agent/tmux where applicable)** is a required part of this Requirement, not merely two Vite variables.

- **One release-level configuration source:** CI/build accepts the column count and Web maximum font size as typed, validated inputs (prefer repository/GitHub Actions Variables or build arguments, using approved defaults if unset). The **same validated column value** is embedded into `web/dist` and carried to the Server runtime; do not maintain independent Web and Server defaults for an identical release. The Web font value remains UI-only but may be recorded in release metadata and optionally exposed as a Server env variable for diagnostics, not used as a PTY font parameter.
- **Server runtime environment:** make `NESSION_TERMINAL_COLS` (proposed name) an explicit **Server process environment variable** written from the build/deploy parameter by the artifact/Compose/GitOps deployment pipeline. `NESSION_TERMINAL_WEB_FONT_SIZE` may mirror the build-selected Web max CSS font size for configuration introspection; Server must not implement its own font sizing policy. The effective values must reach the actual running container/process, not only the temporary CI job environment or a Docker `ARG` discarded after build.
- **Server configuration owner:** follow existing `deploy/entrypoint-server.sh` env → `/etc/nession/config.toml` design and the Server's canonical configuration reader, or choose a single equivalent owner. At startup validate the effective columns and expose them to the Session/Agent boundary that actually controls tmux pane width. A Server-level env var **alone does not resize the Agent-owned tmux pane**; propagate and enforce the chosen column width through the existing authorized control/attach/resize path, with no competing unsequenced channel.
- **Deploy paths:** wire both ordinary `Dockerfile.server` / `Dockerfile.server.prebuilt` consumption and staging/production release pipelines, `deploy/docker-compose.yml`, and GitOps-rendered Server workload environment where relevant. Runtime injection may use an image `ENV`, Compose `environment`, or generated GitOps `env`/ConfigMap, but it must be **traceably produced from the selected build/release parameters**, not a manual post-build edit. Keep staging vs production scopes distinct.
- **Consistency and lifecycle:** record source revision + selected config + artifact identity, verify Web bundle and deployed Server agree on `cols` before admitting a new interactive session. If a browser from a different build joins an existing Session, use existing Session-authoritative cols and an explicit compatibility/reconciliation policy, not a silent pane resize or per-client override. Fail fast for invalid/missing-required values and mismatched releases rather than rendering divergent grids; default handling is documented and deterministic.
- **Standalone Agent:** document what happens without a central Server; if the Agent is the direct PTY owner in standalone mode, it must receive the same canonical columns policy or explicitly obtain the bound Session's width via a verified attach contract. Do not require the Agent to read a Server-only env var that is unavailable in standalone mode.
- **Acceptance evidence:** verify two builds (`80 cols / 13px` and `96 cols / 14px`) from chosen build inputs; check Web emitted config, selected deployment manifest, **actual Server process env and parsed effective config**, and Agent/tmux `stty size`; test invalid values, missing-default fallback, mismatched Web↔Server version, and PC↔phone handoff. Distinguish image build-time values from process runtime env and prove config remains stable when CI variables change without rebuilding/redeploying.

**Repo integration checked:** `Dockerfile.server` embeds a Vite-built Web UI; `release-staging.yml` and `release-production.yml` build Web assets and Server binaries separately and assemble prebuilt images. `deploy/entrypoint-server.sh` derives Server `config.toml` from runtime env; `deploy/docker-compose.yml` supplies the Server env. The implementation must cover both image paths and deployment source rather than only modifying one Dockerfile.
### Prototype

- **Decision:** Required (explicit product request; fixed-column range and mobile readability must be visually compared).
- **Reason / questions:** Which single column count offers acceptable Web typography and a smaller yet usable iPhone display? How does the terminal respond to sidebar collapse, screen/device width, height and mobile keyboard?
- **Scenario:** Select 80/88/96/100/120 or type a column count → inspect side-by-side desktop/iPhone terminal text with **actual browser CSS-pixel font-size** (not enlarged illustration), shared 1:1 fixed-column fixture, live measured cell width, terminal cap and rows → resize viewport/mobile keyboard → same wrap boundaries, changed rows.
- **Status:** Published and **browser-verified on the hosted preview** (2026-10-27). Chromium loaded the Pages preview, exercised every control, and read the rendered CSS font sizes, measured cells, content widths and row counts; gallery, preview and pinned-source links resolve. The Pages CSP blocks the external JetBrains Mono woff2, so the preview uses its disclosed system-monospace fallback and remeasures — the numbers below come from that fallback, not from the production font.
- **Artifact:** shared orphan `prototype` @ [`0fdc5a61bc42e3364a73f8c835c0e6578e96b50e`](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/commit/0fdc5a61bc42e3364a73f8c835c0e6578e96b50e) — [**Hosted preview**](https://bestnathan.github.io/nession/prototypes/terminal-fixed-cols-2487/index.html) (manifest source SHA matches the pin), [Interactive simulator HTML source](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/0fdc5a61bc42e3364a73f8c835c0e6578e96b50e/terminal-fixed-cols-2487/index.html), [prototype README](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/0fdc5a61bc42e3364a73f8c835c0e6578e96b50e/terminal-fixed-cols-2487/README.md), [Gallery index source](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/0fdc5a61bc42e3364a73f8c835c0e6578e96b50e/index.html). The gallery card links to the preview, the pinned source and this Requirement.
- **Browser interaction evidence (hosted preview, Chromium):** baseline 88 cols → Web `14.00px`, App `6.87px`, rows `49 / 75`; 80 cols → `14.00px`, `7.56px`, `49 / 68`; 100 cols → `14.00px`, `6.05px`, `49 / 85`; soft keyboard at 100 cols → App rows `85 → 53`, columns and font unchanged; 120 cols at 1280px with sidebar → Web font `13.12px` (below the 14px cap), rows `40 / 64`, collapsing the sidebar → `14.00px`, `38 / 64`, columns still 120; reset → 88 / 14.00px. Measured wrap boundary always equals the selected column count, content width always equals `cols × measured cell` (673.8px at 80 Web), and computed `transform` is `none` on both terminal screens.
- **Fidelity:** Real DOM/CSS font size and actual browser glyph measurements, fake terminal content/rows; JetBrains Mono via external CSS font asset with system monospace fallback. Not live xterm/VT/tmux/WebSocket, not production Acceptance.

### Interactive prototype — published design artifact

- **Immutable source:** [fixed-column sizing lab at `0fdc5a61bc42`](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/0fdc5a61bc42e3364a73f8c835c0e6578e96b50e/terminal-fixed-cols-2487/index.html). [Source directory](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/tree/0fdc5a61bc42e3364a73f8c835c0e6578e96b50e/terminal-fixed-cols-2487); [Scenario/fidelity notes](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/0fdc5a61bc42e3364a73f8c835c0e6578e96b50e/terminal-fixed-cols-2487/README.md).
- **Controls:** 60–140 cols (80/88/96/100/120 presets), 1280–1920px Web + sidebar toggle, 9–20px Web cap, 393/402/440px iPhone, soft-keyboard row change, TUI fixture/reset/copy JSON.
- **Validated:** files exist on final prototype tip; extracted JavaScript parses successfully; no duplicate HTML element IDs, no missing referenced input IDs; simulated DOM behavior smoke **5/5 passed**; hosted preview HTTPS 200 with `manifest.json` pinning the same SHA; browser click-through verified the controls and measurements above; gallery and README catalog links resolve in the repository and the gallery. No claim of xterm or PTY integration.
- **Local browser:** checkout `prototype`, run `python3 -m http.server 8025`, open `http://localhost:8025/terminal-fixed-cols-2487/`.

### Success Criteria

- [ ] SC-01 A single published canonical column count holds for one live Session across Web/App, foreground takeover, browser resize and relays; PTY / xterm agree on cols, and only rows change with usable height.
- [x] SC-02 Desktop terminal caps at its measured maximum readable width/font; changing sidebar/window width below that cap adjusts actual font metrics to retain exactly the canonical cols without clipping/stretch.
- [x] SC-03 iPhone-sized Web/App viewports use actual smaller CSS font sizes, retain fixed cols and correctly calculate rows through rotation, IME appearance/dismissal and font-load timing; no transient erroneous remote geometry.
- [ ] SC-04 ANSI/TUI output, line wraps, cursor, alternate screen, scrollback and mouse/touch/IME stay correct through PC → phone → PC, local/remote resize ordering and reconnect; distinguish legitimate TUI repaint from horizontal reflow.
- [x] SC-05 Interactive prototype is published to the shared orphan `prototype` branch with pinned immutable source and catalog links; editable columns, Web caps/layout, iPhone presets, visible actual CSS font sizes, calculated row counts and identical fixed-column terminal fixture all respond deterministically to controls.
- [x] SC-06 Canonical design/terminal sizing guidance records the new horizontal sizing rule, superseding only #2286's dynamic columns while preserving its Controller lease, authoritative resize events and Agent safety contract.
- [x] SC-07 Two optional build-time settings independently select the fixed terminal columns and Web preferred/max CSS font size without source changes; omitted values use approved defaults, invalid inputs fail the build, and Web/mobile use the same embedded cols while existing Sessions never silently change width.
- [x] SC-08 The chosen release/build parameters are traceably injected into the **running Server process environment** (including canonical terminal cols) through Compose and staged/production image/GitOps paths; Server validates/reads effective values at startup and the values match the associated Web bundle without manual config drift.
- [x] SC-09 The Server/Agent session sizing owner applies or negotiates the configured fixed columns through the existing ControlLease/authorized resize path, including standalone mode, and prevents mismatched Web↔Server build settings or old attached clients from silently resizing live tmux Sessions.

## Acceptance Plan note (2026-10-27)

The original plan declared every criterion `when: pr`. Pre-merge Case records are evidence-only in this repository: the pre-merge gate requires every `when: pr` criterion to be Pass, and Cases are projected only from merged-SHA runs (the same unexecutable combination repaired for #2300 in #2318 and for #2469 in its plan). All criteria now prove at the merged `staging` SHA; implementation PRs carry source witnesses and Cases run on staging. No criterion text, method, or evidence bar changed.

## Product alignment

- [x] Enables PC↔phone Session continuity without repeated horizontal wraps (VISION).
- [x] Keeps width responsive yet quiet and device-appropriate (PRINCIPLE).
